items.title: Hollywood's Odyssey: The Historians' Verdict
items.description:
Christopher Nolan’s new Odyssey brings Homer’s epic roaring back to life and Tristan Hughes and Dr. Emily Hauser are here to unpack every storm, monster and star-making turn. From the brilliance of the adaptation to the ancient story beneath it, Tristan and Emily bring their expert historical knowledge to challenge what Nolan keeps, what he changes, and why Odysseus still captivates us after 2,500 years.

items.title: Executions at the Tower of London - with Tracy Borman
items.description:
The Tudor period was a particularly brutal time in English history for executions. Many famous royals, courtiers, and clergy were executed at the Tower of London throughout the 16th Century, including Anne Boleyn, Katherine Howard, Lady Jane Grey, Sir Walter Raleigh, and Robert Deveruex.

items.description:

At just 23, Maria Theresa inherited a bankrupt empire, a crumbling army, and a throne every king in Europe was already measuring for his own crown. Within months, Prussia, France, Bavaria, Spain, and more descended like vultures—ready to tear the Habsburg realm apart.

global_silver_linings.title: Heatwave Reveals ‘Lost’ 17th Century Garden Design Under Parched Grass
global_silver_linings.snippet: The outline of a ‘lost’ 17th century garden has been revealed at a stately British home following the record heatwave and long drought. Beneath the parched grass was an ornate garden design being rediscovered after more than 350 years at Chatsworth House in Derbyshire. It turns out, the ornamental arrangement of flower beds and paths […] The post Heatwave Reveals ‘Lost’ 17th Century Garden Design Under Parched Grass appeared first on Good News Network .
global_silver_linings.reason: Even a brutal heatwave can yield something wonderful — parched grass acting like a natural time machine to reveal a hidden garden that's been quietly waiting beneath our feet for 400 years. It's a reminder that history is never entirely lost, just sometimes out of sight.

featured_read.title: Kahlil Gibran on the Art of Becoming Yourself Across the Sweep of Life
featured_read.snippet: A roadmap to the fulfilled belonging on the other side of "the great aloneness which knows not what is far and what is near, nor what is small nor great."
featured_read.blurb: Gibran believed that becoming yourself is less a single awakening than a slow, lifelong crossing through solitude — and this essay traces exactly how he mapped that passage. Set aside the quiet half-hour to sit with his idea that belonging to yourself must come before belonging to anything else.

news.title: Lennox. Manchester: ‘A boot camp of flavours’ – restaurant review
news.snippet: You’ll leave fed, challenged and gastronomically punch-drunk Nico Simeone is the Scottish-Italian chef behind the Six by Nico restaurant empire, and Lennox, in Spring Gardens, Manchester, is his new baby. If you are unfamiliar with Six by Nico, it’s a fever-dream version of fine dining: Simeone conjured up themes such as “The Chippie”, “ Italian Road Trip ” and “ Ancient Rome ”, then served six courses in homage to them. Tokyo!
news.blurb: A restaurant review that promises to leave you pleasantly disoriented, which is frankly the highest compliment one can pay a dining experience.
